title: BWF World Championships Draw Pits Ayush Shetty Against World No. 1 Shi Yuqi as India Hosts
excerpt: India's unseeded rising star faces the tournament's top seed in a blockbuster opener, while PV Sindhu navigates a loaded quarter at the 2026 BWF World Championships in New Delhi.
body:
• India's Ayush Shetty faces world No. 1 and top seed Shi Yuqi of China in a blockbuster first-round men's singles draw at the 2026 BWF World Championships in New Delhi.
  • PV Sindhu, seeded ninth, lands in a loaded section alongside third seed Wang Zhiyi and sixth seed Putri Kusuma Wardani, who eliminated her at the 2025 Worlds in Paris.
  • Lakshya Sen, India's highest-seeded men's singles player at 14th, faces a potentially long road through the bottom half of the draw to reach the later rounds.
  • The tournament runs August 17–23 at the Indira Gandhi Arena, marking the first time India has hosted the BWF World Championships since the event's inception in 1977.

A Tough Opening for Shetty

The draw for the 2026 BWF World Championships, unveiled on Tuesday, handed India's rising star Ayush Shetty a formidable first-round assignment. The 21-year-old, ranked 18th in the world and unseeded, will open his campaign against China's Shi Yuqi, the world No. 1 and tournament's top seed.

Shetty has recent experience against the Chinese ace. At the Badminton Asia Championships in Ningbo in April, Shetty reached the final but was dismantled 21-8, 21-10 by Shi Yuqi. The young Indian will look for a very different outcome on home soil.

"It's the toughest draw you can get, but playing at home in front of an Indian crowd changes the equation. There's nothing to lose."

— Ayush Shetty, speaking to reporters after the draw

Shetty's recent form offers some encouragement. He beat world No. 11 Alwi Farhan 21-17, 5-21, 21-17 in the first round of the China Open last month, a result that showcased his ability to recover under pressure in best-of-three encounters at the highest level.

Sindhu Navigates a Loaded Quarter

PV Sindhu, a two-time Olympic medallist and five-time World Championships medallist, is seeded ninth in the women's singles draw. She finds herself in Section 2 of the top half, sharing a quarter with third seed Wang Zhiyi and sixth seed Putri Kusuma Wardani of Indonesia.

Wardani is a particularly significant opponent. The Indonesian knocked Sindhu out in the quarterfinals at the 2025 World Championships in Paris, winning their three-game encounter 21-14, 13-21, 21-16. A potential rematch could come as early as the third round.

Sindhu, however, arrives in New Delhi riding one of the strongest stretches of form in her career. She claimed the Japan Open Super 750 title in July, defeating defending world champion Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-17 in the final. That win extended her remarkable unbeaten record against Chinese opponents at the Worlds to 8-0.

Sen's Path and India's Doubles Contingent

Lakshya Sen, seeded 14th, occupies the bottom half of the men's draw and is positioned in Section 4 alongside second seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn of Thailand and fifth seed Christo Popov of France. Sen's opening assignment looks manageable on paper, but he could face Vitidsarn, last year's Olympic finalist, as early as the quarterfinals.

In the men's doubles, India's premier pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will carry the nation's strongest medal hopes. The world No. 9 duo reached the quarterfinals at the 2025 Worlds in Paris, upsetting China's Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang along the way.

Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto, who made a historic run to the mixed doubles quarterfinals in Paris—the first Indian pair to reach the last eight in that discipline in seven years—are also in the draw.

A Home Advantage for India

The 2026 BWF World Championships mark the first time India has hosted the tournament. The Indira Gandhi Arena in New Delhi, which also hosted the India Open Super 750 earlier this year, will be configured for approximately 10,000 spectators.

India has won 14 medals at the World Championships historically—one gold, four silver, and nine bronze—with Sindhu contributing three of those (gold in 2019, silver in 2017, bronze in 2013 and 2014). A strong showing on home turf could significantly improve that tally.

What to Watch

The tournament begins on August 17, with the men's and women's singles first rounds. The Shetty-Shi Yuqi clash will headline Day 1, while Sindhu's opener against Singapore's Shuxue Noble should provide a gentler start. The finals are scheduled for August 23, a Saturday, ensuring peak viewership for what promises to be one of the most closely watched editions of the event in years.
